findings.endpoint: acute respiratory tract infection symptom severity
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis reported that Andrographis paniculata was associated with relief of acute respiratory tract infection symptoms compared with controls.
findings.limitations: authors state findings should be interpreted cautiously owing to poor study quality and heterogeneity

findings.finding_summary: The same meta-analysis reported shortened time to symptom resolution in acute respiratory tract infections with Andrographis paniculata.
findings.limitations: authors state findings should be interpreted cautiously owing to poor study quality and heterogeneity

findings.endpoint: common cold symptom intensity (visual analogue scale, day 2)
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of standardized extract SHA-10, symptom intensity including tiredness, sleeplessness, sore throat, and nasal secretion was reported as decreased versus placebo at day 2 of treatment.

findings.endpoint: upper respiratory tract infection symptom severity score
findings.population: patients with uncomplicated upper respiratory tract infection
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of the KalmCold extract in 223 patients, overall visual-analogue symptom scores across nine cold symptoms were reported as significantly reduced versus placebo, with overall efficacy reported as 2.1 times that of placebo.

findings.population: adults with asymptomatic or mild COVID-19
findings.finding_summary: In this double-blinded randomized controlled trial, pneumonia occurred in 0 of 29 participants receiving the extract versus 3 of 28 receiving placebo (p=0.039).
findings.limitations: pneumonia analysis covered a 57-participant subset of the 165 who completed the trial

findings.population: adults with asymptomatic or mild COVID-19
findings.finding_summary: In the same trial, COVID-19 symptoms were relieved by the last day of intervention in both groups with no significant between-group difference reported.
This Cochrane review reported that Pelargonium sidoides may relieve symptoms in acute bronchitis in adults and children and the common cold in adults, while noting that doubt exists.
findings.limitations: authors report substantial heterogeneity across the three adult trials (746 patients) and three child trials (819 children); preparation type was a potential cause, with tablet form not showing an effect

findings.finding_summary: The same Cochrane review reported adverse events were more common with Pelargonium sidoides than comparators, with none classified as serious.

This meta-analysis of 11 randomized placebo-controlled trials (2,195 participants) reported earlier remission of acute cough with extract EPs 7630: at day 5, 56.8% of treated common-cold participants versus 38.8% on placebo showed at least a 50% reduction in cough intensity.
findings.limitations: trials studied the manufacturer's standardized extract EPs 7630; participant counts and day-5 figures confirmed in a follow-up search pass

findings.endpoint: length of hospital stay in COVID-19
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of standardized Brazilian green propolis extract, post-intervention hospital stay was 6.5 ± 6.0 days with propolis versus 7.7 ± 7.1 days with placebo (p=0.22).
findings.limitations: n=188 (98 propolis, 90 placebo); hospital adjunct-treatment context

findings.finding_summary: In the same trial, secondary infection was reported in 6.1% of the propolis group versus 18.9% of the control group.

This systematic review and meta-analysis of five randomised controlled trials reported that bovine colostrum supplementation was associated with a 44% lower incidence rate of upper respiratory symptom days versus placebo over 8-12 weeks.
findings.limitations: 5 RCTs totalling 152 participants, all in exercise-training populations; authors note the low precision of individual study estimates

findings.finding_summary: The same meta-analysis reported a 38% lower incidence rate of upper respiratory symptom episodes with bovine colostrum versus placebo.
findings.limitations: 5 RCTs totalling 152 participants, all in exercise-training populations; authors note the low precision of individual study estimates

findings.endpoint: upper respiratory tract infection symptom frequency
findings.duration: 6 weeks supplementation, effects reported up to 20 weeks
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized controlled trial in pre-school children, six weeks of bovine colostrum supplementation was associated with a 31% reduction in frequency of upper respiratory tract infection symptoms.

findings.endpoint: upper respiratory tract infection symptom severity
findings.duration: 6 weeks supplementation, effects reported up to 20 weeks
findings.finding_summary: The same trial reported a 37% reduction in severity of upper respiratory tract infection symptoms with bovine colostrum versus control.

In this multicentre double-blinded placebo-controlled phase 3 trial (TESTS), 28-day all-cause mortality was 23.4% with thymosin α1 versus 24.1% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.99, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.27; p=0.93).
findings.limitations: n=1106; authors report prespecified subgroup interactions by age (p=0.01) and diabetes status (p=0.04) that warrant further study

findings.finding_summary: In this multicenter randomized trial (ETASS), 28-day mortality was 26.0% with thymosin α1 versus 35.0% in controls (relative risk 0.74, 95% CI 0.54 to 1.02), with significance depending on the analysis (nonstratified p=0.062; log-rank p=0.049).

findings.endpoint: mortality in moderate to critical COVID-19
findings.finding_summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis reported that thymosin alpha-1 therapy may be associated with reduced mortality in moderate to critical COVID-19.
findings.limitations: authors state randomized clinical trials are still required to verify the findings

findings.endpoint: healing of hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers
findings.population: adults with hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers
findings.finding_summary: In this randomized placebo-controlled trial, topical LL-37 treatment was associated with enhanced healing of hard-to-heal venous leg ulcers.
findings.limitations: topical administration in a wound-care context; effect sizes not captured in this batch and pending verification

findings.endpoint: LL-37 expression in chronic ulcer epithelium
findings.finding_summary: This mechanistic study of human skin wounds reported that LL-37 is involved in re-epithelialization and is lacking in chronic ulcer epithelium.
In this randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, complete relief from sneezing was reported by 83% of patients on Tinospora cordifolia, while 79% of the placebo group reported no relief.

findings.endpoint: nasal discharge relief in allergic rhinitis
findings.finding_summary: In the same trial, complete relief from nasal discharge was reported by 69% of patients on Tinospora cordifolia, while 84.8% of the placebo group reported no relief.

findings.endpoint: reports of liver injury with autoimmune features
findings.population: patients at 13 Indian centers using Giloy during the COVID-19 pandemic
findings.finding_summary: This multicenter retrospective case series reported that Tinospora cordifolia (Giloy) use was temporally associated with acute hepatitis with autoimmune features and with unmasking of autoimmune hepatitis in people with silent chronic liver disease.
findings.limitations: retrospective case series, not a controlled trial; causality assessed as probable in 67.4% of cases
